brief.analysis: Defense-and-aerospace versus the broad market is the one pair where the raw and trend-adjusted readings disagree by more than a full step — direct evidence that the average itself is drifting upward, not that price is temporarily stretched above a fixed average. That fits the structural rearmament backdrop (higher NATO and European defense budgets), and the moving-average confirmation is entirely absent (0 of 3, 50-day slope still pointing up) while only 3 of 7 past setups ever reached target. The statistics here are a trap: the mean has moved.
brief.report_line: Avoid shorting defense-versus-market — the trend-adjusted reading diverges from the raw one, signaling the average has structurally drifted up on rising global defense budgets, with no moving-average confirmation and a weak historical hit rate.

brief.analysis: Gold's run against stocks has already snapped most of the way back — the ratio sits near normal and has hit its slower 200-day average, so the easy money is made; only a modest further move is left to reach the 5-year average. The strongest case for a permanently richer gold is heavy central-bank buying and reserve diversification, which likely lifts gold's long-run floor versus equities. But the trend-adjusted read agrees with the raw read (they do not diverge), telling us the average is not running away fast — so the remaining trade is real but small and the old flat average may sit a touch too low.
brief.report_line: Short gold-versus-S&P is largely played out and tradeable in small size toward its longer average, with the caveat that sustained central-bank gold buying may have permanently raised gold's floor and left little juice for a full return to the 5-year mean.

brief.analysis: Chips have run far ahead of the broad tech index and are still very stretched, but the 5-year average sits an implausible ~70% below today's ratio — that target assumes a world before the AI build-out re-rated semiconductors' share of tech growth, and that world is gone. Even measured against its own rising trend the ratio is still rich, so a short toward the 200-day average is defensible as a snap of a real over-extension; anchoring on the flat 5-year average is a trap. Trade the near target only, in reduced size.
brief.report_line: Short chips-versus-tech only toward the 200-day average and half-sized — the AI capital-spending cycle has structurally re-rated semiconductors, making the 70%-lower 5-year average an invalid target.

brief.analysis: Metals-and-mining ran ahead of the market and has already snapped back to its 200-day average, with the trend-adjusted read matching the raw read (no divergence), so the underlying average looks stable and the reversion is genuine. The offsetting risk is a real structural bid under miners from high gold prices and copper-electrification demand, and the historical evidence is thin — only two prior episodes, both of which worked. Tradeable as the snap continues, but size down and don't lean fully on the 5-year average.
brief.report_line: Short metals-and-mining-versus-market is a confirmed snap-back to its longer average worth trading in reduced size, tempered by a thin two-episode track record and a structural bid under miners from gold and copper demand.

brief.analysis: Silver spiked far ahead of gold and has already reverted most of the way, hitting its 200-day average, with the trend-adjusted read confirming the raw read (no divergence) — evidence the underlying relationship's average is stable, not drifting. Silver's industrial and supply-deficit story is a genuine structural bid, but silver-versus-gold is historically volatile and reliably mean-reverting, and the extreme stretch has largely unwound. Clean, high-conviction reversion with a solid forward hit rate.
brief.report_line: Short silver-versus-gold is a clean reversion that has already reached its longer average and is confirmed by trend-adjusted readings; the main watch-item is silver's structural industrial deficit, which argues against pressing beyond the 5-year mean.
